name: hindi-nonprofit
description: A well-built Delhi literacy NGO site (Sakshar Delhi Foundation) written entirely in Hindi (Devanagari), lang="hi", category nonprofit_institution, with English URL slugs as most Indian sites have. The non-Latin coverage fixture: everything language-neutral must pass (structure, dates, phone, JSON-LD, identity, links, FAQ by question headings), and the checks that depend on English phrase lists must be gated to low confidence, never asserted at full strength.

expected.notes: Category nonprofit_institution at medium confidence from NGO JSON-LD and the /donate and /programs URL patterns; the Hindi nav labels score nothing, which is the honest result. Roles are found from the English slugs (/about, /programs, /news, /contact), so the absence gate does not fire and every key fact is actually checked. Three of the four key facts are language-neutral and present: mission from the NGO description, programs_or_services from the four Hindi h2 headings on /programs, location from the PostalAddress. how_to_participate depends on the English participation vocabulary and is absent although the site says 'दान करें' on every page; key_fact_missing therefore fires at medium (one fact) and the language gate caps it at low confidence with language_scope hi. The hero check is the same: no English category noun in the lead, one signal, gated. en.cta.missing is not_evaluated (language_not_supported) rather than a false 'no call to action'. NAP passes on the phone (+91 11 2690 7400) because the Devanagari address has no grammar yet; the name component is not graded because the brand name has no Latin letters. The FAQ passes on three Devanagari question headings; continuity passes because Hindi words are tokenised as whole words (combining marks kept), which is what the tokenizer fix guards.
